runtime_validity.runtime_audit_scope: Candidate review verifies observed version bindings; executable-copy and replacement lineage validation belong to the separate panel audit.

findings.detail: The final rename predicate treats any missing extensionless path as a directory. Moving an ordinary extensionless file such as notes or README produces a nonexistent old path with no extension and therefore a Catalog nudge. This conflicts with ordinary-file quietness. The added test checks only the existing destination notes.txt, which does not cover this sequence. This source-based finding was not executed; the five-case score remains unchanged, and the runtime-version violation independently makes this original run invalid.

limits: Static candidate review, not a proof of complete correctness.
Tool request inspection is not a complete operating-system access audit; a reply without an error marker does not independently prove successful access.
The candidate review is static; additional retrospective diagnostics are retained separately. The original scored checker and acceptance scores were not changed.
Original create-then-write coverage is reported separately from the prospectively added atomic-import requirements.
One historically unstable permissions test was excluded identically before scoring; candidates introduced no additional exclusions.
broader_observations: The reviewed changes target directory arrivals. Broader removal or move-out behavior was not exercised by the five-case checker and is not counted as a candidate defect here.

A proposed repeated-directory test without an intervening catalog reread was withdrawn before execution: another nudge may be validly coalesced, while a fresh reader can receive the existing two-second debounced notification within the four-second bound. Historical implementation differences alone did not establish a defect.

static_findings.detail: A separate once-per-revision public-API test atomically imports a chat deeper than the new scan limit but inside the catalog depth bound. The candidate times out at the saved four-second notification wait after the unconditional fresh catalog assertion proves the chat is visible. The historical reference and all eight effective A/C candidates pass. Frozen five-case scores remain unchanged.

The new scan has per-directory bounds but no shared total-work limit, so work can multiply across directory levels while running in the shared watcher callback. Its initial path.is_dir/read_dir follows a symlink supplied as the event path, although recursive child entry.file_type checks do not follow symlinks. No directory contents are emitted by the patch; these are unexecuted filesystem-read and latency concerns, separate from the executor tool-path audit.

The scan takes only 1,024 unsorted entries per directory without a fallback notification if truncated, while the catalog permits a larger global entry set. This entry-count limit was not exercised by the depth diagnostic.
